scope: execution path decision per implemented demo

1.description: Existing test instance plus an own synthetic training database.

2.description: Pure T-SQL control inside an isolated test instance.

3.description: Containerised single instance for provisioning or reproducible CPU and memory limits.

4.description: Hyper-V virtual machine for Windows, operating system, storage or isolation requirements.

5.description: Multi-instance or network topology for a distributed core statement.

escalationRule: The smallest sufficient stage applies. Every entry above stage 2 must name the rejected lower stage and the technical reason why it is insufficient.

instanceRequirementModel.SHARED_TEST_INSTANCE: The demo may run on a test instance that is shared with other green demos.
instanceRequirementModel.DISPOSABLE_INSTANCE: The demo requires an instance that may be reset or discarded.

provisioningNote: This catalogue records the required execution path. It does not provision an environment and is not an input to automated environment creation.

demos.title: SARGability
demos.rationale: Predicate forms, access methods and logical reads are observable in a single session against an own synthetic database.

demos.title: Statistics Anatomy
demos.rationale: Statistics header, density vector and histogram are read from the own synthetic database without changing server state.

demos.title: Plan Properties
demos.rationale: Plan-wide and operator-level properties are read through session-scoped plan access; no server-level feature is switched.

demos.title: Rebind, Rewind, Outer References and Spools
demos.rationale: Rebinds, rewinds and the optimizer-chosen performance spool are visible in the actual plan of a single session.

demos.title: Slow in Application, Fast in Tooling
demos.rationale: The two client profiles are executed one after another as separate sqlcmd phases, and cache evidence is read object-scoped for a single demo procedure.

demos.title: Classic and Dynamic Search Conditions
demos.rationale: The three strategies run sequentially in one session, and plan reuse evidence is read object-scoped inside the marker-owned demo database.

demos.title: Parameter Sensitive Plan Optimization
demos.rationale: The optimisation is switched at database scope inside the marker-owned demo database, and dispatcher and variant evidence is read marker-scoped from the plan cache of a single session.

demos.title: Optional Parameter Plan Optimization
demos.rationale: The database scoped configuration is switched inside the marker-owned demo database only, and dispatcher, optional predicate and variant evidence is read marker-scoped from the plan cache of a single session.

demos.title: Controlled Spill
demos.rationale: The spill is forced through memory grant control in T-SQL, but it loads tempdb of the whole instance and therefore must not run next to unrelated work.

demos.title: Blocking Chain
demos.rationale: Four client sessions against one isolated instance produce the blocking chain; the participant can start them manually in four windows. Held locks make the instance unusable for unrelated work during the run.

demos.title: Query Store History
demos.rationale: Query Store is enabled only in the marker-owned synthetic database and is removed with that database after the history has been observed.

demos.title: Bounded Extended Events Evidence
demos.rationale: The server-scoped event session is marker-filtered, memory-bounded and reversible, but an isolated disposable instance prevents interference with unrelated event-session administration.
